title: Powerdevil does not provide a way to inhibit display turn-off
line: Apps can now keep the display from turning off, even on the lock screen, without blocking screen locking or sleep.
explanation: PowerDevil's PolicyAgent only knew two inhibition types: sleep (InterruptSession) and idle (ChangeScreenSettings). The idle one also blocks dimming and is what apps use to stop screen locking, and PowerDevil deliberately ignores it once the screen is locked, so there was no way to keep only the display on (e.g. for HDMI audio, which stops when the monitor sleeps). The change adds a third type, TurnOffDisplay (value 8, listed as "display" in RequestedInhibitions/ActiveInhibitions), which only stops the DPMS action from turning the display off, also while locked; idle inhibitions still imply it while unlocked, so existing behaviour is unchanged.

commits.message:
daemon: add an inhibition type to only keep the display on

Apps could only inhibit idle as a whole, which also blocks locking, and
idle inhibitions stop counting once the screen is locked. Add a display
type that stops the display from turning off, also on the lock screen.

BUG: 369129

media.caption: Master: an app holds AddInhibition(8, ...) and the display is still turned off after the 30 s timeout (black).
With the fix: same inhibition, the desktop is still on after 45 s idle.
Master: screen locked with the same inhibition, the display turns off after the 15 s locked timeout.
With the fix: the lock screen activates normally and stays visible after 45 s.

reviews.text: Clean, minimal implementation of a dedicated TurnOffDisplay (value 8, "display") PolicyAgent inhibition type that blocks only DPMS display turn-off without inhibiting dimming, locking, or sleep, and remains active while the screen is locked. Existing ChangeScreenSettings (idle) inhibitions continue to imply TurnOffDisplay only while unlocked, preserving current behavior. D-Bus introspection docs, PolicyAgent state/notification handling, and DPMS integration are consistent and thoroughly verified.
